subject: paediatrics
title: Neonatal resuscitation and stabilization: NRP steps

steps.tx: Every birth needs a trained team, a preheated **warmer** and tested equipment ready before the baby arrives. The team dries, warms and stimulates the baby, then positions the head in the **sniffing position** to open the airway. Assessment of tone and breathing decides the next step, and the **Apgar score** never delays resuscitation. Delayed cord clamping for 30 to 60 seconds suits a vigorous baby.
steps.say: A trained team prepares the warm bed and checks every device before delivery. The team dries the baby and provides warmth while giving gentle stimulation. Positioning the head correctly opens the airway for breathing or ventilation. Doctors judge tone and breathing effort to decide what help comes next. The numerical score recorded later never delays the urgent first steps.

steps.tx: **Positive pressure ventilation** starts when the baby is apnoeic, gasping or has a heart rate under 100. The team gives 40 to 60 breaths each minute and watches for visible **chest rise** with each breath. When the chest fails to rise, the **MR SOPA** steps correct mask position, airway and pressure in order. Term babies start with room air while oxygen rises by preductal targets over the first minutes.
steps.say: The helper ventilates the baby when breathing is absent or the heart beats too slowly. Each breath should lift the chest visibly in a regular and controlled rhythm. A fixed sequence of corrective steps can solve most failures of chest movement. The right hand gives the reading that guides oxygen use after birth. Oxygen concentration then rises gradually toward the target for each minute.

vis.caption: Neonatal positive pressure ventilation (PPV) technique and monitoring

steps.tx: Chest compressions start when the heart rate stays **under 60** after 30 seconds of effective ventilation. Two thumbs encircle the chest and compress the lower sternum by about one third of its depth. The team follows a **3 to 1 ratio** and raises oxygen to 100 percent during compressions. **Adrenaline** by the intravenous route and volume expansion treat a rate that still stays low.
steps.say: Compressions begin when good ventilation alone fails to raise the heart rate enough. Both thumbs press the lower breastbone while the fingers support the back. Three compressions alternate with one breath in a steady coordinated cycle. Pure oxygen replaces room air once compressions become necessary during resuscitation. A vein in the cord then provides the route for emergency medicine.

steps.tx: This illustration shows the **two thumb encircling** technique on the lower third of the sternum, with fingers supporting the thorax from behind. An **umbilical venous catheter** with a syringe sits ready for adrenaline or volume. The picture matters because compressions follow effective ventilation when the heart rate stays under 60. For the exam, link this hand position with the 3 to 1 compression and ventilation ratio.
steps.say: Both thumbs will press the lower part of the breastbone in the centre of the chest. The fingers of both hands support the back and steady the whole thorax. This grip gives controlled compressions without tiring the rescuer too quickly. A catheter in the cord vein stands ready for emergency drugs and fluids. The image will fix the correct hand position that examiners often ask about.

vis.alt: Illustration of gloved hands giving two thumb sternal compressions to newborn with umbilical venous catheter and syringe shown.
vis.caption: Illustration showing two thumb chest compressions and umbilical venous catheter. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: After resuscitation the team guards temperature within **36.5 to 37.5** and screens the baby for **hypoglycaemia** without delay. Babies at risk of infection receive antibiotics, and selected babies with brain injury meet criteria for cooling. Counselling supports parents when resuscitation starts near **22 to 25 weeks** of gestation. A team debrief and clear records close the golden hour of stabilisation.
steps.say: The team keeps the baby warm and checks the blood sugar soon after resuscitation. Signs of infection lead to early antibiotics and close observation in the unit. Selected babies with possible brain injury receive controlled cooling under strict criteria. Parents receive honest counselling when birth occurs at the border of viability. The team later will review its actions and record every important step.
